items.title: Pope Leo XIV has lung cancer, Vatican says, after successful surgery
items.summary: NPR and CBS News report that the Vatican said Pope Leo XIV had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on 13 October and that pathology showed lung adenocarcinoma. The Vatican says the roughly 90-minute operation had no complications and recovery is proceeding as normal, with about a week expected. Oncologists quoted by CBS call the prognosis excellent because it was caught early.
items.why: A leader's health news forces careful, transparent communication, a live case study in crisis and stakeholder communication.

items.title: Riots reported in Albania's capital as students join anti-government movement
items.summary: ABC News' international page lists riots in Tirana as students joined an anti-government movement, alongside flooding in Istanbul with at least two deaths. These come from a section page rather than full articles and are not precisely dated, so treat details as provisional.
items.why: Youth-led protest movements reshape political risk and brand sentiment in a market, relevant to any firm operating abroad.

items.title: Supreme Court issues notice to Rahul Gandhi and Congress over INDIA bloc march to the court
items.summary: Business Standard reports the court issued notices on a petition seeking limits on political protests inside court premises, after the INDIA bloc's 12 October march demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Bar and Bench reports a wider batch of petitions on the electoral-roll revision before a bench led by CJI Surya Kant.
items.why: Court rulings on protest and election rules shape the political calendar that employers and brands plan around.

items.title: Sensex surges 1,534 points to 74,316 as crude falls and IT stocks lead
items.summary: Business Standard reports the Sensex closed 2.11% higher at 74,315.61 on 15 October, and Kotak Securities puts the Nifty at 22,997.35, up 1.66%. Both credit IT and auto stocks, crude oil down about 2% and a stronger rupee; broader markets ended weaker than the headline indices.
items.why: Falling oil eases input costs and inflation worries, which lifts spending confidence and corporate budgets.

items.title: Jio Platforms sets up India's biggest IPO, around Rs 30,000 crore, opening 21 October
items.summary: Business Today and a Groww digest report a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119, anchor bidding on 19 October, subscription from 21 to 23 October and listing expected on 28 October. Reports put the issue at about Rs 28,755 to 30,213 crore and the valuation near Rs 10.3 lakh crore. Sources are news and aggregator reports, so size and dates are provisional.
items.why: A record IPO is a major brand and investor-relations event, and it shapes hiring and marketing budgets in telecom and digital.

items.title: Jio Platforms reported FY26 revenue of Rs 1,46,885 crore and profit after tax of Rs 30,049 crore
items.summary: An IPO analysis report cites these FY26 figures from the offer documents. They come from a secondary source and are provisional.
items.why: Scale and margin numbers like these decide how a company is valued and how it positions itself to investors.

items.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon reported available for long-running agent work
items.summary: A 15 October AI digest says Google released Gemini 4 Argon through the Gemini API and AI Studio with introductory pricing, plus a Gemini app task mode that keeps working while you are away. Earlier reports said Google was limiting Argon to vetted cybersecurity experts, so the access picture conflicts and is provisional.
items.why: Agentic AI that works unattended changes how HR and marketing teams plan routine analysis and content work.

items.title: Anthropic reported to launch Claude Haiku 5.5 for fast, high-volume tasks
items.summary: The same digest reports Claude Haiku 5.5 aimed at summaries, database queries, customer support and coding sub-agents. This rests on a single newsletter, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: Cheaper, faster models widen where AI is affordable, including support and screening workflows in HR.

items.title: Workday made its Sana assistant the main agentic interface for HR, finance and IT
items.summary: The 15 October AI digest reports the change, a signal that HR software vendors are putting AI agents at the front of their products. Single-source and provisional.
items.why: HR tech is moving to agent-first interfaces, which is directly relevant to an HR specialisation.
